candidates: When renaming an exported type (or any public symbol), verify whether it has ever been exported via `package.json` exports maps, re-exported from barrel files, or documented as public API before deleting the old name. If there is any risk of downstream consumers using the old name, retain it as a `@deprecated` alias (e.g., `export type OldName = NewName;`) until a deliberate deprecation cycle is complete.

When building an array by mapping user-provided IDs against a record/dictionary (e.g., `ids.map(id => index.entries[id])`), filter out `undefined` results for keys that are absent rather than using a type assertion to suppress the undefined type. Use `.filter((entry): entry is T => entry !== undefined)` or `flatMap` to produce a clean, type-safe array and avoid silent runtime errors downstream.

After calling `options.presets.apply(...)` for a preset whose return value will be immediately used (e.g., methods called on it), validate that the result is non-null/non-undefined before proceeding. If the preset is required, throw a descriptive error immediately at the point of retrieval rather than letting a `TypeError: cannot read property of undefined` surface later at the call site.

Apply consistent error handling to the same async call regardless of the code path it appears in. If a call (e.g., `storyIndexGenerator.getIndex()`) is wrapped in try-catch with a safe fallback in one place (such as an `onInvalidated` callback), it must be equally guarded in every other place it is called (such as initial store setup). Asymmetric protection leaves initialization exposed to the same failure mode the callback protects against.

When a request-response pattern is implemented by subscribing to terminal events (e.g., run-completed, fatal-error, cancel), always add a timeout that calls `unsubscribe()` and sends an error/timeout response if no terminal event arrives within a reasonable deadline. Without a timeout, stalled or hung runs cause the subscriber to accumulate indefinitely, leaking memory and leaving callers waiting forever.
